SPACE CRAFT JOURNAL / CEILINGS & SERVICES

Step into the future trends of office ceiling design.

Treat the ceiling as part of the whole room. This Space Craft planning note looks at step into the future trends of office ceiling design through the choices that affect everyday use, the details worth testing and the questions to take into your project brief.

Space Craft editorialPlanning note · 4 min read
IN THIS NOTEStart with the services above itCompare systems by useCoordinate the room belowMap activity before assigning desksBefore you decide
01 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Start with the services above it

A ceiling has to work around lighting, ventilation, fire services and access requirements. Establish the existing constraints and coordinate specialist advice before choosing a finished pattern.

02 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Compare systems by use

A suspended grid may offer practical access; a continuous finish can create a quieter visual field. Review repairability, acoustic performance and the effect on available height, using product-specific information.

03 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Coordinate the room below

Align the ceiling and lighting with the furniture arrangement, not just the outline of the room. Recheck the setting when partitions, meeting tables or workstations move.

04 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Map activity before assigning desks

Write down the tasks people perform, how often teams overlap and when visitors arrive. A desk count alone will not reveal the need for private calls, project tables or storage.

BEFORE YOU DECIDE

Take this into your brief.

  • Survey existing height and service locations.
  • Ask how maintenance access will be provided.
  • Review a sample and a reflected ceiling plan together.

Write down one priority, one constraint and one question you still need to answer. Review them beside the plan or material sample before agreeing the next design decision.

General design considerations for discussion. Product suitability, technical performance, statutory requirements and project pricing need appropriate, project-specific review. Images are illustrative.
